title.narrative: Indonesia Sustainable Landscape Management and Marine Plastics Innovation Hub

description.narrative: This investment provides grants to: 1) The World Bank's Sustainable Landscape Management Multi-Donor Trust Fund aiming to address the drivers of unsustainable natural resources management; and 2) CSIRO's Marine Plastics Innovation Hub aiming to address the issue of plastic waste through partnership and collaboration between research, entrepreneurship, and investment.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Australia supported Greenhope, an Indonesian start-up to participate in the CSIRO-implemented Indonesia Plastics Innovation Hub. The start-up develops and markets biodegradable plastics from cassava starch. Cassava is a renewable source abundantly available in Indonesia and its high starch content is ideal for biodegradable and compostable packaging. The Plastics Innovation Hub has provided technical advice and mentoring to further improve the technology to produce commercial-grade cassava-based plastics. The collaboration and networking opportunities extended by the hub also support Greenhope’s quest to accelerate the adoption of sustainable practices and innovative solutions. To date, Greenhope has successfully replaced 12 billion pieces of conventional plastic with biodegradable plastic and improved the welfare of 179 Indonesian cassava farmers along the way.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Mangroves sequester carbon and protect coasts from increased erosion due to climate change. Carbon sequestration by mangroves is up to 10 times greater than mature tropical forests. Mangroves store 3-5 times more carbon per equivalent area than tropical forests (Coastal Blue Carbon - NOAA). Indonesia has the second largest expanse of mangroves globally. ‍ Australia through The World Bank-managed Sustainable Landscape Management Multi-Donor Trust Fund (SLM MDTF) supports the Indonesian Government to develop a regulation for integrated mangrove management and require government agencies at national and sub-national levels, and relevant stakeholders to coordinate towards common objectives. ‍ The policy will strengthen mangrove management across Indonesia. It will: ‍ -delineate roles for strategic planning, management, and supervision of mangroves; ‍ -define the range of activities permitted in mangroves; ‍ -set-up controls on mangrove degradation; ‍ -distribute roles between national and sub-national governments; and ‍ -acknowledge the role of coastal communities in mangrove management.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Sustainable Landscape Management Multi-Donor Trust Fund (SLM-MDTF) supported a new approach for engaging communities in mangrove restoration through the Mangroves for Coastal Resilience (M4CR) project. The project engaged over 6,000 individuals in a cash-for-work scheme to rehabilitate 13,344 hectares of mangroves. The project also introduced Mangrove Stewardship Village (Desa Mandiri Peduli Mangrove/DMPM), which integrates mangrove management into village-level activities, creating a more community-driven approach. To do so, the project delivered capacity-building activities in over 50 villages, supported the integration of mangrove management into 15 village regulations, and facilitated the issuance of social forestry permits (securing land use rights) in 59 villages. This approach advances inclusive, sustainable mangrove management, allowing community to benefit from livelihood opportunities associated with mangrove products, and from better protection against climate-related storms and erosion.

description.narrative: The Sustainable Landscape Management Multi-Donor Trust Fund (SLM-MDTF) supported agriculture input subsidy reform through the design and preparation of a direct assistance-to-farmers pilot project. This US$ 8 million pilot initiative, to be jointly implemented by the World Bank and Indonesia’s Ministry of National Planning (BAPPENAS), aims to test the proposed reforms. By directing subsides more efficiently and empowering farmers, the reform is expected to increase public spending efficiency, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from rice cultivation and fertilizer use, and contribute to the government’s food security agenda.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Sustainable Landscape Management Multi-Donor Trust Fund supported the preparation of restoration plans for 41,428 hectares of mangroves. By the end of 2024, 13,344 hectares of mangroves had been rehabilitated. This rehabilitation is expected to contribute to slowing biodiversity loss and contribute to Indonesia’s emission reduction from the land use sector under its Forest and Land Use (FOLU) Net Sink 2030 agenda. To ensure long-term impact from the planning and planting activities, trained local community groups will monitor the mangrove areas to measure ecological outcomes.
